uncited: The method consists of two coupled models: a **Main Model** (standard TensoRF) and an **Augmented Model** (Simple-TensoRF).
The Augmented Model is trained with reduced capacity to prevent it from learning complex, noisy artifacts.
Its predicted depth is then used to regularize the Main Model.
*   Main Model: High-quality rendered images and accurate depth maps.
*   Augmented Model: Regularized depth maps used for supervision.
*   Density Tensor Components ($R_\sigma$): Number of rank-1 components for density.
*   Color Tensor Components ($R_c$): Number of rank-1 components for color features.
*   Grid Resolution ($N_{vox}$): Resolution of the voxel grid for tensor decomposition.
*   Bounding Box ($b$): Defined as $b = (b_{x1}, b_{x2}, b_{y1}, b_{y2}, b_{z1}, b_{z2})$.
*   MLP Depth ($D$): Depth of the small MLP for color decoding.
*   View-dependent layers ($l_v$): Number of view-dependent layers.
*   Density Components ($R_{\sigma s}$): Reduced number of components.
*   Grid Resolution ($N_{vox}^s$): Reduced voxel grid resolution.
*   Bounding Box Z-min ($b_{zs1}$): Increased (shifted inward) Z-min to exclude near-camera artifacts.
*   Mass Concentration Intervals ($N_{mc}$): Number of intervals for entropy loss.
*   Initialize Main TensoRF with full capacity parameters.
*   Initialize Augmented TensoRF with reduced capacity parameters.
*   Train the Augmented Model for a subset of iterations (e.g., first 5,000 iterations) or concurrently, depending on implementation.
*   Compute depth estimates from the Augmented Model.
*   Filter these depths to identify "reliable" estimates.
Initial LR: $2 \times 10^{-2}$ (tensor), $1 \times 10^{-3}$ (MLP).
*   **Block Artifacts:** Reducing only the grid resolution ($N_{vox}$) allows the model to learn sharp changes in density ($\sigma$) at voxel edges, causing block artifacts.
Reducing only the number of components ($R_\sigma$) causes small, completely opaque floaters.
*   **Near-Camera Distortions:** Reducing the bounding box size (specifically $b_{z1}$) helps mitigate objects incorrectly placed close to the camera.
However, applying this reduction to the *main* model can distort objects that are truly close to the camera.
*   **Transparent Floaters:** Significant transparent floaters may persist in the main model, particularly in regions visible in only one training view.
*   **Strengths:** Significantly improves depth estimation accuracy and reduces floaters compared to vanilla TensoRF and DS-TensoRF.
*   **When to Use:** When training TensoRF with very few input views (e.g., 3-10 views) and depth accuracy is critical.

*   **When Not to Use:** When computational resources are extremely limited (due to 2x training time) or when the scene contains many transparent objects that require specialized handling beyond mass concentration.
The method addresses the issue of shape-radiance ambiguity and floater artifacts that arise when factorized tensor models like TensoRF are trained on sparse data.
